pairs.question: How can I stay motivated to quit smoking?
pairs.answer: Keep a list of reasons to quit handy for motivation. Focus on how your life will be better when you no longer smoke.

pairs.question: Is it okay to cut back on smoking instead of quitting all at once?
pairs.answer: Yes, cutting back on smoking over time can be a helpful strategy as you approach your quit date.

pairs.question: How can I prepare for my quit day?
pairs.answer: You can prepare by picking a quit day in the future and working toward it. This gives you time to plan and gather support.

pairs.question: What are some common feelings people have about quitting?
pairs.answer: Many people are worried or afraid of quitting, as they see smoking as a central part of their lives.
pairs.evidence: It’s common for people to think they can’t function without smoking. And it’s also normal to be worried about or afraid of quitting.

pairs.question: I feel really stressed right now. Should I wait to quit smoking until things calm down?
pairs.answer: Quitting smoking can actually reduce stress in the long run. There’s no drug in cigarettes that magically gets rid of stress, so it’s something you’ll have to deal with regardless.
